_meta.purpose: Declares who actually governs this repository, so that every other governance artifact can be checked against the truth rather than against an aspiration.
_meta.why_this_exists: M29-H established that this repository has exactly one account with any access, and that account authors every commit. The governance prepared in M29-A through M29-E assumed more than one human: required_approving_review_count is 1, require_code_owner_review is true, and FINANCE may not be the repository owner. Applied as-is to a sole-owner repository those rules do not produce strong governance, they produce a repository nobody can merge into — and a CODEOWNERS requirement pointed at an inert file, which is the M29-A defect exactly. Declaring the mode makes the gap a recorded fact with a validator behind it, instead of a surprise discovered at the first blocked pull request.
_meta.the_distinction_that_matters: Deferred is not satisfied. SOLE_OWNER does not weaken a single automated control — lint, static analysis, tests, migrations, Redis, financial concurrency, secret scanning, dependency audit and workflow integrity all remain required and all still gate a merge. What it defers is the part that needs a second human to exist. The validator says so out loud on every run rather than reporting green and letting the reader infer four-eyes review that is not happening.
_meta.no_synthetic_participants: AI assistants are tools, not participants. Claude and ChatGPT contributed code to this repository and neither is, or may be represented as, a collaborator, code owner, independent reviewer, release actor, bypass actor or human approver. The validator rejects any such handle in any identity slot. A fabricated second reviewer would satisfy every check in this repository and defeat the entire purpose of the review it simulates.
how_to_move_to_multi_person: 1. Add a second real human with write access to the repository.
2. Set mode to MULTI_PERSON here and record them under human_participants.
3. Create .github/governance/identities.json from identities.example.json with real handles; FINANCE must not be the repository owner.
_meta.organization_migration: Supported and explicitly deferred. Teams (@org/team) require an Organization; owner.type is currently User, so CODEOWNERS may name individual usernames only and actor_type Team is unavailable.

active_controls: stale review dismissal on new commits
production tag immutability, no bypass actor

deferred_controls.reason: The repository has one human participant. GitHub forbids approving your own pull request, so required_approving_review_count above 0 would block every merge rather than cause a review.
deferred_controls.resolves_when: a second real human is granted write access

deferred_controls.reason: Every rule in .github/CODEOWNERS is commented out and every owner is an unresolved <OWNER:...> placeholder. Enabling require_code_owner_review against that file either blocks every pull request or enforces nothing, and which one is not obvious until somebody tries to merge — the defect M29-A was opened to remove.
deferred_controls.resolves_when: identities.json holds real handles and verify_governance_identities.php reports READY FOR ACTIVATION

deferred_controls.reason: M27 split finance permissions by consequence so that one person could not both write and approve a change that moves money. With one human that separation cannot exist. It is recorded as absent rather than marked satisfied.
deferred_controls.resolves_when: a second real human owns FINANCE and is not the repository owner
compensating_controls: every settlement and rollout flag ships false
financial scheduled work is registered disabled
the financial concurrency gate runs on every pull request
settlement.execute requires the M28 exit gate before it may be enabled
